title: Platform systems & services: ops playbook, how-tos, dashboards, runbooks, retrospectives & roadmap (Q2 2027)
author: Michael Chen
content:
Overview

This document is the canonical operations playbook for the Platform Systems & Services team. It consolidates: system and service ownership, repeatable how-tos, dashboard and alert definitions, primary runbooks for common incidents, a short retrospective of the last two quarters, and the team roadmap for Q2 2027. Intended audience: platform engineers, SREs, on-call engineers, and product stakeholders.

Goals

- Provide a single, searchable reference for oncall and runbook procedures.
- Standardize dashboards and alert thresholds across critical platform services.
- Capture actionable retrospective items and map them to roadmap work.

Contents (quick links)

1) Systems & services inventory and ownership
2) How‑tos (deploys, canaries, emergency rollbacks)
3) Dashboards & alerts (queries, thresholds, example panels)
4) Runbooks (network, GPU capacity, degraded model serving)
5) Recent retrospectives: incidents & learnings (Q3 2026 — Q1 2027)
6) Roadmap (Q2 2027 priorities)
7) Wiki and operational hygiene

1) Systems & services inventory and ownership

Short inventory of high‑impact services (owner team + primary pager):

- platform-api (owner: platform-api service team; pager: platform-oncall-engineering)
- runtime-router (owner: serving-runtime; pager: runtime-oncall)
- kv-cache-service (owner: serving-runtime; pager: runtime-oncall)
- batch-orchestrator (owner: infra-scheduler; pager: infra-oncall)
- metrics-collector (owner: observability; pager: observability-oncall)
- auth-proxy (owner: security-infra; pager: security-oncall)

SLOs (top-level):

- platform-api: availability 99.95% (p30), p99 latency < 120ms for 0–1024 tokens
- runtime-router: availability 99.9%, tail latency p99 < 250ms for short inference requests
- metrics-collector: availability 99.9% for ingestion pipeline

Ownership matrix: each service has an owner, a primary oncall rotation, and an escalation path (service lead -> platform manager -> head of platform). Update owners via PR to /eng-platform/team-wiki/ownership.csv.

2) How‑tos (deploys, canaries, emergency rollback)

Standard deploy (CI -> canary -> prod):

1. Create PR against main and include changelog and rollforward instructions.
2. CI runs unit tests, integration smoke tests, and e2e on a canary namespace.
3. Trigger canary rollout: kubectl apply -f deploy/canary.yaml --namespace=canary
4. Monitor canary panels for 15 minutes: error rate, p95 latency, JVM/gpu memory.
5. If stable, promote with: kubectl apply -f deploy/stable.yaml --namespace=prod

Canary test checklist (must pass before promotion):

- 0 production error rate spike > 0.5% over baseline
- p95 latency degradation < 10% relative to baseline
- No increase in 5xx from downstream integrations

Emergency rollback procedure:

1. If critical alerts trigger (see runbooks), open an incident and set status on the incident channel (#incidents).
2. Execute rollback: kubectl rollout undo deployment/<svc> -n prod --to-revision=<previous>
3. Post-rollback validate: smoke tests + synthetic traffic validation (scripts/synthetics/validate.sh)
4. Notify customers via status page and create postmortem.

Common CLI snippets

- Promote canary: kubectl set image deployment/platform-api platform-api=registry.redwood/v1.2.3 -n prod
- Check pod restart counts: kubectl get pods -o wide --sort-by=.status.containerStatuses[0].restartCount
- Tail logs: stern platform-api -n prod --since 15m

3) Dashboards & alerts

Dashboard naming convention: Platform / <service> / <topic> (example: Platform / runtime-router / Latency & Errors)

Critical dashboards (panels and queries)

- Platform / runtime-router / Latency & Errors\  - Panels: p50/p95/p99 latency (by route), 5xx error rate, request throughput\  - Example metric query (PromQL): rate(http_server_requests_seconds_count{job="runtime-router"}[1m]) / rate(http_server_requests_seconds_sum{job="runtime-router"}[1m])

- Platform / GPU Fleet / Utilization & Queue\  - Panels: GPU utilization per node, queued inference requests, OOM count\  - Example query: avg_over_time(gpu_utilization{cluster="prod"}[5m])

- Platform / Metrics / Ingestion Health\  - Panels: tail latency to TSDB, dropped metrics, consumer lag

Alert definitions (examples)

- runtime-router_high_error_rate
  - Condition: 5m sliding window error rate > 2% AND absolute errors > 50 requests/min\  - Severity: P1 (page)
  - Pager: runtime-oncall
  - Runbook: see runbooks/runtime-router-high-error-rate (section 4)

- gpu-fleet_node_max_utilization
  - Condition: GPU utilization > 92% for 5m on > 20% of nodes\  - Severity: P2 (notify)
  - Pager: infra-oncall

- metrics-ingestion_lag_high
  - Condition: consumer_lag_seconds > 300s for any critical topic\  - Severity: P1

Alert tuning guidance:

- Use both relative and absolute thresholds to avoid noisy pages for low traffic services.
- Escalate to P2 for capacity issues; only P1 for user-visible degradation or data loss.

4) Runbooks (copy this section to incidents channel when page is used)

A. runtime-router — high error rate (P1)

Symptoms

- p95 latency jumps, 5xx rate > 2%, service 5xx count > 50/min

Immediate steps

1. Triage: run the preflight checks (kubectl get pods, describe failing pods, check recent deploys)
2. If recent deploy in last 30 minutes, rollback that deploy (see How‑tos)
3. Check downstream services (kv-cache, model backends) for increased latency/503s
4. If cache miss storms detected, enable emergency KV protective policy: POST /admin/kv-cache/limit {"mode":"protective"} (internal admin API)
5. If CPU/GPU pressure is root cause, scale replicas: kubectl scale deployment/runtime-router --replicas=<n> -n prod and monitor
6. Engage runtime-oncall -> service owner -> head of platform as escalation if unresolved after 30 minutes

Post-incident

- Run the incident checklist, capture timeline, and create a postmortem within 72 hours. Assign action items.

B. GPU fleet — capacity saturation (P2 -> escalate if customer impact)

Steps

1. Check scheduler queue: kubectl get jobs -n inference-queue
2. Validate autoscaler logs (k8s-autoscaler) for failures to provision nodes
3. If autoscaler healthy but queue remains, create emergency capacity: terraform apply -target=module.gpu_pool -var='size=+10' (runbook-approved creds required)
4. If provisioning fails due to cloud quota, open support case and apply temporary burst policy: policy/burst-capacity (internal guide)

5) Recent retrospectives (Q3 2026 — Q1 2027)

Summary of notable incidents and learnings:

- Incident: runtime-router cache miss storm (Nov 2026)\  - Root cause: cache TTLs lowered in a release; load increased by a spike in synthetic traffic.\  - Actions: add pre-deploy synthetic load regression checks; implement protective KV policy; update canary checklist to include cache telemetry

- Incident: metrics-ingestion lag (Jan 2027)\  - Root cause: downstream TSDB compaction job overloaded ingestion consumers during peak\  - Actions: add consumer backpressure, increase ingestion partition count, add alert for consumer_lag_seconds>120s

Retrospective action items (status):

- Add synthetic regression harness to CI (owner: eng-developer-experience; ETA: 2027-03-01) — DONE
- Add protective mode for kv-cache (owner: serving-runtime; ETA: 2027-01-15) — DONE
- Rework alert thresholds for low-traffic services to include absolute minima (owner: observability; ETA: 2027-02-28) — IN_PROGRESS

6) Roadmap (Q2 2027 priorities)

Roadmap items (quarter objectives):

- Objective A: Improve inference tail latency and reliability\  - Deliverable: per-model prescriptive kernel profiles for top-10 models (owner: serving-runtime; target: 2027-04-30)\  - Deliverable: rollout of predictive autoscaling (model-aware) for runtime-router (owner: infra-scheduler; target: 2027-06-15)

- Objective B: Reduce on‑token cost via caching & batching improvements\  - Deliverable: prefix-awareness for KV cache to increase hit rate by 12% (owner: serving-runtime; target: 2027-05-15)\  - Deliverable: dynamic batch sizing pilot for high-throughput customers (owner: platform-api; target: 2027-06-01)

- Objective C: Operational excellence and developer experience\  - Deliverable: unified dashboard templates and alert library (owner: observability; target: 2027-04-15)\  - Deliverable: runbook automation (playbooks -> run incidents -> runbook assistant) pilot (owner: eng-platform; target: 2027-06-30)

Roadmap dependencies and risks

- Depend on infra budget for additional GPU headroom during predictive autoscaler validation.
- Risk: backward-incompatible runtime changes require coordinated Dedicated/Private deployment communications.

7) Team wiki and operational hygiene

This page is the canonical ops playbook. Related operational artifacts should live under the team wiki (updates via PR):

- /confluence/eng-platform/platform-team-wiki-runbooks-dashboards-roadmap-2027-q2 (living runbook index)
- /confluence/eng-platform/ownership.csv (owners map)
- /confluence/eng-platform/oncall-rotations.md (current oncall schedule and run escalation play)

Housekeeping guidance

- Add a reviewer and label for any change that affects alerts or runbooks.
- Small runbook edits can be merged without a full review; alert threshold changes require 2 reviewers including observability lead.
- Archive dashboards older than 12 months unless marked as "long-term".

Appendix: useful links and snippets

- Synthetic validation script: scripts/synthetics/validate.sh- kubectl snippets and stern logs commands (see How‑tos)
- Incident template: /confluence/incident-response/incident-template

If anything in this document is unclear or out-of-date, please raise an issue in the eng-platform channel and submit a PR to update this page.
